primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to UMOD (ADTKD-UMOD)
mechanism: Pathogenic UMOD variants impair uromodulin folding and cause abnormal uromodulin accumulation in the endoplasmic reticulum of thick ascending limb cells, producing a renal-limited endoplasmic-reticulum storage disease and progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
vignette: A 29-year-old man is evaluated for slowly progressive chronic kidney disease. Urinalysis shows no hematuria and minimal protein. He had his first episode of gout at age 19. His father and paternal grandmother both developed chronic kidney disease with similarly bland urine sediment. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in UMOD.
lead: Which of the following cellular abnormalities best explains this patient's kidney disease?
correct: Retention of misfolded uromodulin in the endoplasmic reticulum of thick ascending limb cells
distractors: Failure to assemble the type IV collagen network in the glomerular basement membrane
Defective lysosomal degradation of cystine in proximal tubular cells
Loss of vasopressin-regulated aquaporin insertion in collecting-duct principal cells
Defective cleavage of polycystin proteins in renal tubular primary cilia
distractor_notes: Type IV collagen defects cause Alport syndrome, which is a glomerular basement-membrane disorder characterized by hematuria rather than the bland urinalysis of ADTKD-UMOD.
Cystinosin defects cause cystinosis with proximal tubular dysfunction/Fanconi syndrome, not autosomal dominant UMOD-associated tubulointerstitial disease.
Defective aquaporin-2 trafficking causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with impaired urinary concentration rather than inherited progressive tubulointerstitial CKD with early hyperuricemia/gout.
Polycystin dysfunction causes autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with renal cyst formation rather than the ER-storage mechanism of ADTKD-UMOD.
key_expl: ADTKD-UMOD is an endoplasmic-reticulum storage disease. Most pathogenic UMOD variants disturb uromodulin folding, leading to intracellular retention/accumulation of abnormal uromodulin in thick ascending limb cells and progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
objective: Explain ADTKD-UMOD as a thick-ascending-limb endoplasmic-reticulum storage disease caused by abnormal uromodulin folding and retention.
